title: Researcher workspace
intro: Load your own export from a platform, decide what happens to each part of it, and see what participants will see. Your export stays in this tab: it is not stored and not sent anywhere. Only the structure and your decisions are kept in this browser as a draft.
exportsIntro: Add your own or a synthetic export. You can add several, for example in different languages; their structure is combined.
filesIntro: Save your work as structure.json and importer.json, or open files saved earlier or shared by another project.
confirmStartOver: This clears the structure and all decisions in this workspace. Have you saved your files? Continue?
started: Here is the structure of your export, with a table for every list. Everything starts undecided, which participants see but are not asked to donate.
opened_one: Opened. {{count}} setting is waiting for a path that is not in the structure yet.
opened_other: Opened. {{count}} settings are waiting for paths that are not in the structure yet.
openFailed: These files could not be opened: {{reason}}
pending_one: {{count}} setting waits for a path no export has shown yet. It is kept and saved.
pending_other: {{count}} settings wait for paths no export has shown yet. They are kept and saved.
onlyUndecided: Only show what is still undecided
selectHelp: Choose a name in the tree to give it a label, a description or aliases.
leafHelp: A field. Choose whether participants see it, are asked to donate it, or whether it is ignored.
innerHelp: A group of fields. Ignoring it ignores everything inside.
label: Label
descriptionHelp: One sentence, used when we ask for this field, for example “the time you watched each video”.
raw: Donate the value as it is in the file, not converted
aliasesHelp: Other names that mean the same, such as a translation (kijkgeschiedenis.json) or a renamed key. Use * as a wildcard.
badRegex: That is not a valid regular expression.
mergeHelp: If this is the same as another part next to it, merge it: its name becomes an alias and what is inside is combined.
merged_one: Merged. {{count}} setting differed on both sides; the one you merged into was kept.
merged_other: Merged. {{count}} settings differed on both sides; the ones you merged into were kept.
mergeTogether_one: Not merged: both parts are in one of your loaded exports, so they hold different data.
mergeTogether_other: Not merged: both parts are in {{count}} of your loaded exports, so they hold different data.
previewIntro: The tables participants will see with your current decisions, filled with your own export.
previewEmpty: Add an export to see the preview.
noTables: With these decisions, participants would see nothing yet.
tableHelp: The entries of this become the rows of a table. Its label is the table's name. Tables inside its rows show up as a number participants can open.
keysHelp: Are the keys here data rather than names of fields, such as the people who replied or the days of a diary? Then each key becomes a row, with the key and its value as columns.
keysAreData: The keys here are data: each key is a row of a table with a key and a value column.
keysDecisionHelp: The decision here is about the keys themselves, such as the names of the people who replied.
confirmKeys: All keys here become one position, and their names are not kept, because they are data. Decisions that differ between them are listed afterwards. Continue?
recordTable: Fields that are not part of a list
undecidedOnly: Only fields that are still undecided
shortcuts: Keys on a selected row: 1 undecided, 2 ignore, 3 show, 4 donate.

viewHelp.fields: Only tables and the fields in them, named as their columns. Hover a field to see where it is in the file.
viewHelp.tree: Everything in the files, including the folders, objects and HTML in between.

chartIntro: Count rows over time or per value, from the exports you loaded. This runs in your browser; it is a first step towards views participants can make themselves.
readAsHelp: How the value is read. Participants see, and donate, the value as read here.
cleanHelp: Cleaning steps, applied in order before the value is read.
filterHelp: Rows must meet every condition here. Use it to leave out rows that are not the participant's own activity, such as ads.
filterExclude: Leave out the rows that meet this instead
suggestIntro: These parts are new, and sit where a part you already have is missing. They may be the same thing, renamed or in another language. Merging keeps your decisions and adds the new name as an alias.
required: Required: an upload only fits when this is there
requiredHelp: Any of its names counts, so a merged or aliased part is satisfied by either name. Use it for parts every export has; a participant without them cannot add their data.
newChildrenAsk: Read, show and ask about them
newChildrenHelp: Skipped parts are never opened, shown or offered for structure sharing. That keeps uploads small and the questions short, but you will not hear about renamed or new parts here.
findTitle: Finding the export in a bigger upload
findHelp: Participants pick their export as a zip, a folder or a file, and that is tried first, without looking at its name. If it does not fit, Combray looks inside it for files or folders with one of these names, such as Takeout or watch-history*.json. Use * as a wildcard; letters can be upper or lower case.

problem.too-many-files: This upload has more files than Combray looks through. Pick the export itself.
problem.too-big: This upload is larger than Combray reads in a browser.

rootHelp: The upload itself: the file, folder or zip a participant picks, without its name. Below are the settings for matching uploads to this tree.
handoffFailed: That sign-in from the key page has been used or has expired. Sign in here instead.
noProjects: You are not a member of any project yet. Ask the server operator to add you.
projectNoAccess: waiting for a colleague to give you access
keysElsewhere: Opening donations and managing keys happen on the key page, with your passkey.
signInTitle: Sign in to the researcher workspace
signInIntro: Sign in to work on your projects. We email you a code; this browser then stays signed in for 30 days.
accountsBy: Researcher accounts are created by your server operator or by a colleague on a project.
codeSent: If there is a researcher account for {{email}}, a code is on its way. Type it here, in this browser. It works for 10 minutes.
devOutbox: This is a development server: it does not send mail, but writes it to a folder (.dev/outbox).
anotherCode: Use another address or send a new code
codeWrong: That code is not right, or it has expired. Check it and try again, or ask for a new code.
tooMany: Too many attempts. Please wait a while and try again.
mailDisabled: This server cannot send email yet. Ask the server operator to set it up.
signInFailed: Signing in did not work. Please try again.
projectNotFound: This project is not one of yours
